بَالٍ [act. part. n. of بَلَاهُ; Trying, proving, or testing. ―
-b2- And hence,] Knowing, or being acquainted [with a thing]; as in the phrase, جَعَلْتُهُ بَالِيًا بِعُذْرِى I made him to be acquainted with my excuse, and to know the manner thereof. (Mgh.) ＝
-A2- Also Old, and wearing out [or worn out]; applied to a garment. (Msb.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] بَالِيَاتٌ is used as meaning The places of tents. (Ham p. 492.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
